title: The Firm That Sold 'Lifetime' Light Bulbs—Then Made Them Die in a Year
hook: A cartel of light bulb manufacturers secretly agreed to shorten bulb life so you'd buy more—and buried the evidence for nearly a century.
why_this_can_go_viral: Reveals a secret, decades-long conspiracy that affects every viewer's wallet and evokes outrage at corporate manipulation.

title: The Trader Who Crashed a Stock by Spreading a Rumor He Started Himself
hook: He shorted a company, then paid bots to tweet a fake scandal—and walked away with millions before anyone realized the lie was his.
why_this_can_go_viral: Exposes how easily markets can be rigged with fake news, tapping into distrust of social media and finance.

title: The Startup That Invented a 'Revolutionary' Battery—It Was a Potato in a Box
hook: They raised $30 million from top VCs for a breakthrough battery. The prototype? A potato connected to a light bulb.
why_this_can_go_viral: Absurd yet true—viewers love stories of audacious fake-tech frauds that fooled wealthy investors.

title: The Monopoly That Bought Every Train Track—Then Let Routes Rot for Profit
hook: One company owned the rails and deliberately delayed trains so you'd pay more for trucks—while infrastructure crumbled.
why_this_can_go_viral: Reveals how monopolies weaponize decay to maximize profit, a hidden system that affects supply chains globally.

title: The Spy Who Stole a Company's Secret Algorithm—By Bribing a Janitor
hook: A rival firm paid a cleaning crew to photograph whiteboard notes at night—and stole a billion-dollar trading formula.
why_this_can_go_viral: High-stakes, low-tech spy story that feels like a Hollywood heist—viewers love the 'invisible insider' angle.

title: The Factory That Sold 'Fresh' Lobster—It Was Chicken Soaked in Fish Oil
hook: A seafood distributor dyed and flavored chicken legs to pass as lobster meat in restaurants for years.
why_this_can_go_viral: Gross, shocking, and relatable—everyone eats out and will question what's really on their plate.

title: The Industry Cover-Up of a Chemotherapy Drug That Sped Up Cancer
hook: A pharmaceutical giant knew its flagship drug accelerated tumor growth—but hid the data for 12 years to keep selling it.
why_this_can_go_viral: Combines life-or-death stakes with corporate betrayal—triggers fury and fear, ensuring massive engagement.

title: The Trader Who Used a Fake Diplomatic Pouch to Smuggle Stock Tips
hook: He stuffed insider trading notes into a sealed embassy bag, immune from customs—until a bored officer opened it.
why_this_can_go_viral: Bizarre real-life loophole story with a 'caught red-handed' climax—perfect for short-form suspense.

title: The Startup That Claimed AI Could Detect Lies—It Was a Guy with a Lie Detector
hook: They pitched 'revolutionary AI polygraph' to investors; the AI was just a man in a back room watching a cheap machine.
why_this_can_go_viral: Satirical yet true—exposes the hype bubble around AI, making viewers feel both amused and smarter.

title: The Spy Who Infiltrated a Rival's Boardroom by Being Their Barista
hook: A competitor trained a barista to work at a coffee chain inside a corporate HQ—and sold every conversation to the enemy.
why_this_can_go_viral: Juicy, low-tech spy story set in an everyday setting—makes viewers paranoid about casual chats.

title: The Ad Campaign That Hijacked Your Brainwaves to Sell You Snacks
hook: A chip brand used EEG headsets at a mall to detect when you were hungry—then played ads that triggered cravings.
why_this_can_go_viral: Creepy, sci-fi level manipulation that feels dystopian—viewers love to hate and share these revelations.

title: The Corporation That Paid a Scientist to 'Prove' Asbestos Was Safe for Kids
hook: An asbestos giant funded a study that claimed children were immune to lung damage—the data was completely fabricated.
why_this_can_go_viral: Combines child endangerment with cold corporate fraud—maximum darkness and moral outrage fuel shares.

title: The Trader Who Used a Smoke Signal System to Beat the NYSE in 1900
hook: Before radio, a trader paid Native Americans to send smoke signals from hilltops—giving him prices 20 minutes early.
why_this_can_go_viral: Fascinating, forgotten piece of history that feels like a clever heist—nostalgic and educational.

title: The Startup That Faked a Celebrity Endorsement—with a Deepfake Video
hook: They used AI to make Elon Musk pitch their crypto app on Instagram—real users invested $2 million before the lie broke.
why_this_can_go_viral: Taps into AI fear and crypto skepticism—viewers love seeing how easily tech can be weaponized to steal.

title: The Monopoly That Owns All the Seed Patents—Then Made Farmers Pay Every Year
hook: A biotech giant patented life itself: farmers who saved seeds were sued into bankruptcy—and forced to buy anew annually.
why_this_can_go_viral: David vs Goliath story with moral outrage—affects global food supply, making it universally relevant.

title: The Ad Campaign That Used Voice-Activated Billboards to Trigger Your Panic
hook: A billboard heard your car window down and played a screaming sound—making you look in terror at the product being advertised.
why_this_can_go_viral: Creepy, intrusive, and feels like a Black Mirror episode—viewers will share in horrified fascination.

title: The Industry Cover-Up of a 'Green' Pesticide That Killed Bees—and Children
hook: A chemical giant knew its 'eco-friendly' pesticide caused neurological damage in kids—but rebranded it as safe for 20 years.
why_this_can_go_viral: Mixes environmentalism, health, and corporate betrayal—a triple threat for viral outrage.

title: The Startup That Sold 'Carbon Neutral' Credits—It Was Planting Weeds in a Desert
hook: They claimed to offset millions of tons of CO2 by 'reforesting' barren land—the trees died, and they just kept selling credits.
why_this_can_go_viral: Exploits a hot topic (climate) with a scandalous 'Emperor's New Clothes' angle—activists and skeptics both share.
